scenario: WIBTA for selling what I receive in my dad's will? | Obligatory "I'm on mobile, so sorry for mistakes." I (22M) have a very large family. Both of my parents have 3 kids from past relationships, and I'm the only child they have together. My dad (71) never divorced his previous wife, but has been with my mom (61) for the past 25 years. My dad is a severe alcoholic and has a bunch of other health problems. So the talk of his will has come up a few times. He owns the house we currently live in, his (separated) wife's house, and a bar that has 2 apartments above it. As of now, his wife's house would remain her's or if she passes, go to their 3 children. The house we live in now, would be split amongst the 4 of us. The bar and the apartments would go solely to me. My mom is worried she won't get anything when he does pass away, so she constantly asks if I'll give her half of the bar. I personally want nothing to do with the bar due it being a cause for my parent's alcoholism. My mom says I should just give it all to her if that's the case. I would ask her to at least buy out my half, but she has been mentally abusive to me for most of my life, and constantly sabotaged anything I've done to try and better my own life. I've recently thought about just selling my quarter of the house to my siblings, and the entire bar to them or anyone else who wants it. WIBTA if I decided to leave my mom out of anything I get from my dad's will?

prediction.raw: **1 (Not an asshole)** **Why:** - **Inheritance is not a obligation**. You are not legally or morally required to share your inheritance with anyone, especially someone who has been mentally abusive and actively sabotaged your life. The will explicitly states the bar and apartments go solely to you, and your mom has no claim to it (she’s not named in the will, and she’s not legally married to your dad). - **Abuse changes everything**. Mental abuse and sabotage are serious harms. You have every right to protect your emotional well-being and boundaries. "Giving" to someone who has consistently hurt you could enable further manipulation or harm *yourself*. - **"Leaving her out" is accurate**. The will already excludes her entirely—she’s not a beneficiary. Your role is simply to *not* change that. If you choose to sell your share to siblings or others (or keep it all), that’s your decision. - **No "asshole" behavior here**. You’re not being unfair or entitled—you’re setting boundaries to preserve your own health. In fact, *not* giving her anything is a healthy, self protective choice. **Important note:** - Consult a lawyer about the will’s validity (e.g., if your dad’s mental state is compromised due to alcoholism, or if your mom could legally contest it). Your well-being comes first. 💙 - *If* you * want* to help your mom (e.g., if she genuinely needs support), consider *voluntary* assistance outside of inheritance (e.g., therapy resources, not money), but only if it’s safe and sustainable for you. **You owe her nothing.** - **Final verdict: 1 (Not an asshole)**. You’re doing the right thing by prioritizing yourself.
